scope: Primary-source reading supporting a data-only research agenda; no imported images, runtime data changes, model knowledge tests, or image generation.

sources.title: Getty AAT — About the AAT
sources.supports: Concept records distinguish equivalence, hierarchical and associative relations and retain notes and sources.
sources.limit: A vocabulary model informs authoring; it does not establish LLM knowledge or image-model behavior.

sources.title: Getty AAT — Scope Note
sources.supports: A scope note specifies one contextual concept, qualifiers distinguish homographs, and related meanings require explicit boundaries.
sources.limit: The proposed concept-card structure is this report's adaptation, not a Getty requirement for this project.

sources.title: Getty AAT — Multilingual Equivalency
sources.supports: Concept equivalence requires more than literal translation; broader, narrower and partly overlapping terms need distinctions.
sources.limit: Every Korean, Japanese or English expression still needs domain and language review.

sources.title: V&A — Madeleine Vionnet: an introduction
sources.supports: Bias cutting concerns grain direction and affects fabric drape; construction and visible result are related but distinct.
sources.limit: A draped appearance alone does not prove bias-cut manufacture.

sources.title: The Museum at FIT — Bias cut
sources.supports: Historical garment examples link bias cutting and drape in the 1930s.
sources.limit: Exhibition examples do not prescribe one silhouette for every bias-cut garment.

sources.title: V&A — Corsets, crinolines and bustles
sources.supports: Different support garments and historical variants involve distinct structural elements such as boning, busks and lacing.
sources.limit: A silhouette does not prove hidden construction, and period examples should not become universal modern requirements.

sources.title: CottonWorks — Mesh
sources.supports: Mesh has open spaces between yarns or loops, providing a structural distinction from a printed grid.
sources.limit: Mesh does not imply one transmission level, layer owner, garment use, or model moderation outcome.

sources.title: Schneider-Kreuznach — Split Diopter GEN2 fact sheet
sources.supports: A split diopter enables a near focus plane through the diopter and a far plane through the uncovered area.
sources.limit: A generated image cannot establish actual lens hardware; a visible soft transition is not universally mandatory.

sources.title: Kodak — Essential Reference Guide for Filmmakers
sources.supports: Film/base reflections can create secondary exposure around bright objects; antihalation layers reduce it (PDF pages 32 and 200, zero-based).
sources.limit: This supports local highlight behavior, not an assertion that every halation effect must be red.

sources.title: Getty AAT — Contrapposto
sources.supports: Asymmetric weight distribution and balancing body axes distinguish contrapposto from merely relaxed standing.
sources.limit: A single statue's arm arrangement should not become a universal requirement; partial crops may hide necessary evidence.

sources.title: Barrett et al. (2019) — Emotional Expressions Reconsidered
sources.supports: Facial movements vary with people, culture and context and do not uniquely establish an emotion or mental state.
sources.limit: The article does not define fictional character archetypes; project scene definitions require their own scope.

sources.title: Ghosh et al. (2023) — GenEval
sources.supports: Fine-grained text-image alignment can be separated into object co-occurrence, position, count, color and attribute binding.
sources.limit: This report uses those dimensions to design data cases; it does not adopt or run the benchmark's automated evaluator.

sources.title: Huang et al. (2025 revision) — T2I-CompBench++
sources.supports: The revised benchmark distinguishes attribute binding, object relationships, numeracy and complex compositions.
sources.limit: Benchmark results for other models do not measure this skill or its current image model.

sources.title: OpenAI — ChatGPT Images 2.0 system card
sources.supports: Safety screening can act on text, input images and generated outputs; neutral vocabulary alone is not an acceptance guarantee.
sources.limit: The card cannot identify why a particular local historical request was blocked or which single word caused it.
